narrative:
The model determined that you have a 56% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income. 

Your credit history of "all paid at bank" was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. This is quite rare—only 2.9% of approved applicants share this history, while most have either existing paid credits or critical/other credits. Combined with your checking account showing a negative balance (something only 12.6% of approved applicants have), these two factors created a significant negative impression.

Working in your favor was your very low installment rate of 1% of disposable income, well below the 3% average among approved loans. This helped reduce the risk score, but unfortunately not enough to overcome the concerns from your credit history and account status.

The bank suggests you focus on improving your checking account balance and building a stronger, more typical credit history through consistent on-time payments. Once these areas show clear improvement, reapply for a smaller loan amount with a longer repayment period to increase your chances of approval.
